title: The money files that drew a no vote
question: Which contracts, leases, grants and appropriations did at least one supervisor vote against at the final vote, and how close was it?
finding: 124 money files drew at least one no at their final vote from 2015 to 9 November 2026. 3 were voted down: file 141301 (Appropriation - Cost of Doing Business for Non-Profit Agencies - General City Responsibility - …), 5 to 6 on 3 March 2015; file 151182 (Sale of City Property - 30 Van Ness Holdings, LLC - 30 Van Ness …), 4 to 7 on 8 December 2015; file 230915 (Amended and Restated Office Lease - Retroactive - The Lighthouse Building LLC - 1155 …), 0 to 11 on 26 September 2023. 10 more passed with a margin of three votes or fewer. At the other end, 81 of the 124 had a single no, and 47 belong to same-day lists on which one member voted no to every file (all 9 of those lists fall on a day the Board voted on the annual budget ordinance, with the same member voting no on it). One more belongs here but is not counted, because the minutes print its final passage twice: file 160358 (Appropriation and De-Appropriation - Surplus Revenue and Expenditures - Supporting Increased Overtime …): printed twice: 6 to 5 (noes: Avalos, Campos, Cohen, Kim, Peskin), then 7 to 4 (noes: Avalos, Campos, Kim, Peskin), so it passed over at least 4 noes whichever is the vote on record; it is set out on the screen about the hole in the record.
how: Every money file whose final Board roll call prints at least one No, closest margin first and, within a margin, largest title amount first. The file number links to the vote page, or to the minutes of the meeting where the vote was read from the minutes. “What it is” is the opening of the title, at most 25 words. “Files on the same vote list” counts money files decided that day on the identical line-up of votes. The party and the amount of every row shown were read against the full title by hand.
limits: A no vote is ordinary and says nothing against the organization named: the vote pages give no reasons, and dissent can be about the policy, the procedure or the budget as a whole (17 of these 124 titles approve something retroactively, 3 set competitive bidding aside, and 42 are appropriation or budget ordinances). Of the 770 files of $10 million or more introduced since 2019, 650 carry a report by the Board’s Budget and Legislative Analyst among their attachments, so a vote with no dissent can follow written scrutiny at the committee stage. Parties that are private persons or family trusts are not named. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. “Excused” is printed for a member who was out of the room or away as well as for one excused from voting; the page does not say which, and it is never read here as anything else. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
